extracted.intended_audience: published prose (fiction + creative nonfiction) and poetry writers applying for the NEA Creative Writing Fellowship
extracted.subtask_description: Selection criteria for the NEA Creative Writing Fellowship: a blind, text-only evaluation of a submitted writing sample (prose or poetry) judged for artistic excellence and merit. Guidance is aimed at applicants preparing samples for an anonymous panel review.

rubrics_metrics.name: The artistic excellence and artistic merit of the submitted writing sample
rubrics_metrics.description: "The artistic excellence and artistic merit of the submitted writing sample."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the single, controlling selection criterion. Evaluation is blind (panelists see only the writing sample, no name/bio). The NEA emphasizes that quality is judged on the text itself rather than the writer's biography or pedigree; therefore submissions should demonstrate excellence without relying on external context. A robust rubric should apply to a text-only sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level mastery
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panelists explicitly consider command of sentence craft — clarity, precision, rhythm, syntactic control, and the micro-level choices that shape voice and meaning. Applicable in a blind/text-only review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators look for an individual, recognizable voice that distinguishes the work. Because review is anonymous, voice must emerge from the text alone and not depend on external biography or publication venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong imagination
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample should demonstrate imaginative power — compelling ideas, inventive images, or original conceptual leaps that engage readers and convey creative vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-taking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panelists reward work that takes aesthetic or formal risks rather than relying on safe, conventional choices. Because panels change year-to-year, acceptable risks may vary with panel tastes; nonetheless demonstrated boldness in the writing is a positive factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Achieved formal control
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft and structure should be disciplined and deliberate — the writer must show control over form (e.g., structure, pacing, use of poetic/device choices) so that imaginative risk and voice are effectively realized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resonance and depth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should have emotional, intellectual, or thematic depth that lingers with the reader; surface cleverness without depth is less likely to meet this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample should offer fresh perspectives, novel approaches, or distinctive combinations of elements that set it apart from familiar or derivative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous/text-only review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymous review (panelists see only the writing sample, no name/bio)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because review is blind and based solely on the text, applicants should ensure their submission is self-sufficient: avoid relying on reputation, prior publication info, or metadata to convey merit. Panelists are different each year and diverse in geography, race/ethnicity, and artistic POV, so clarity and strength in the sample help across varying tastes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program eligibility and genre cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: $50,000 awards to published prose (fiction + creative nonfiction) and poetry writers; two-year cycle: prose one year, poetry the next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit under the correct genre for the fellowship cycle (prose vs. poetry). The program targets published writers; applicants should confirm eligibility and submit material appropriate to the announced genre/year.
